True parts: no server-version check exists in preflight.py or config.py, and a `mysql+<anything>` scheme (e.g. mysql+asyncmy) passes the `scheme.startswith("mysql")` branch at preflight.py:139. False part: preflight.py:180-183 raises PreflightError 'unsupported database scheme (expected sqlite/postgres/mysql)' for any scheme outside those three, so non-MySQL schemes such as mariadb:// or oracle:// are rejected, and sqlglot_dialect_for_url (safety/readonly.py:178-190) returns None for them. The prior evidence was wrong about the harm. In the head readonly.py, _DENIED_UNION (541-543) is built as _ALWAYS_DENIED_FUNCS unioned with every _SIDE_EFFECT_FUNCS value, MySQL's included. _ALL_CATALOG_SCHEMAS (205-207) and _ALL_CATALOG_NAME_PREFIXES (208-210) are likewise built from every _CATALOGS_BY_DIALECT value, MySQL's included. _denied_funcs (554-561) and _catalog_names (213-218) return these unions for an unknown or None dialect. A guard hole fixed in the MySQL entry therefore flows into the unknown-dialect fallback automatically. Only a fix made to a Postgres or SQLite entry would not, and AGENTS.md.src 19-20 forbids adding to those. The 'change the MySQL branch only' bullet that the finding quoted is no longer in the head AGENTS.md.src. A search of AGENTS.md.src for 'MySQL branch', 'per-engine' and 'per-dialect' finds only line 14, which describes the legacy per-dialect branches and does not direct changes to a single branch. Lines 19-20 say new guards and fixes target MySQL only and add nothing to the legacy engine code. I searched the head view for readers of that rule and found no other source of it. No carve-out is needed, and the rule does not leave the union path open.
